scenes.heading: Using graphs to solve problems
scenes.sub: Let the graph give you the answer
scenes.say: When do two phone plans cost the same? When does a fast car catch a slow one? Draw the graphs, and the answer is where the lines cross.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Ali catches Ben on a walking track: same time, same place
scenes.science: Two lines cross: same x, same y
scenes.breaks: Real walkers speed up and stop, but our straight lines assume a steady speed the whole time.
scenes.say: Ali starts at the gate. Ben starts thirty metres ahead but walks more slowly. Graph their distances against time and you get two lines. The moment Ali catches Ben is where the lines cross: same time, same distance.

scenes.heading: Solve with a graph
scenes.question: Use the graph of y = 2x + 1 to solve 2x + 1 = 7.
scenes.say: To solve two x plus one equals seven, draw y equals two x plus one and the flat line y equals seven. They meet at three, seven. Read down to the x-axis: x equals three.
scenes.caption: To solve 2x + 1 = 7, draw y = 2x + 1 and the flat line y = 7. They meet at (3, 7). Read down to the x-axis: x = 3.

scenes.heading: Solving 2x + 1 = 7 by graph
scenes.say: First the line y equals two x plus one, then the flat line y equals seven. They meet at three, seven. Drop down to the x-axis and read the solution: x equals three.
scenes.caption: y = 2x + 1 meets y = 7 at (3, 7), so the solution is x = 3.

scenes.heading: Which bike hire?
scenes.question: A: $30 + $5 per hour. B: $10 per hour. When are they equal? Which is cheaper for 8 h?
lines: Same at 6 h ($60); A cheaper at 8 h
scenes.say: Company A charges thirty dollars plus five an hour. Company B charges ten an hour. The lines cross at six hours, sixty dollars, so they cost the same then. After that, B's line is higher, so for eight hours A is cheaper: seventy dollars against eighty.
scenes.caption: A charges $30 plus $5 an hour. B charges $10 an hour. The lines cross at 6 hours, $60. After that, B's line is higher, so for 8 hours A is cheaper: $70 against $80.

scenes.heading: Where the costs cross
scenes.say: Here are both bike hire lines. A starts at thirty dollars and rises gently. B starts at zero but rises faster. They cross at six hours and sixty dollars. After that, B is the higher line, so A is cheaper.
scenes.caption: A and B cross at (6, 60). After 6 hours, B is higher, so A is cheaper.

scenes.heading: What the numbers mean
points: Gradient = the rate (per hour, per km)
scenes.say: In real graphs, say what the numbers mean. The y-intercept is the starting value, like a fee. The gradient is the rate, like dollars per hour. The crossing point is where both are equal. And on a cost graph, the lower line is cheaper.

scenes.heading: Distance–time graphs
scenes.say: On a distance–time graph, the gradient is the speed. A line rising two hundred and forty kilometres in three hours means eighty kilometres per hour. Steeper means faster. A flat section means the distance isn't changing, so the object has stopped.
scenes.caption: On a distance–time graph, the gradient is the speed. A line rising 240 km in 3 hours means 80 km/h. Steeper means faster. A flat section means the distance isn't changing, so the object has stopped.

points: Solve by finding where lines meet
Steep is speedy, flat is stopped
scenes.say: Quick recap. Where lines cross, both quantities are the same. You can solve equations by finding where lines meet. The gradient is the rate and the intercept is the start. Steep is speedy, flat is stopped. Now try the practice questions!
